rows.notes: The cited document is a review article (Reviews of Geophysics, 'Ground, Proximal, and Satellite Remote Sensing of Soil Moisture') that synthesises the literature on soil moisture measurement, retrieval and root-zone estimation; it does not report its own experiment or dataset on remote sensing delivering crop production outcomes. It only discusses, citing others (e.g., Ines et al. 2013, Han et al. 2016, Chakrabarti et al. 2014), that SM information can feed crop growth models, irrigation scheduling and yield forecasting (section 9.2), and identifies SSM-to-RZSM estimation as a remaining grand challenge (section 10). A few illustrative in-house comparisons (e.g., Figure 10 GPS vs SMAP, Figure 17 lab evaporation column) are incidental and not about the claimed effect. Q1 is 'no' because the study is a review, so Q2-Q9 are 'no'.

Same document: a review, not a primary study. It discusses applications of SM information for drought monitoring, flood and landslide forecasting and agricultural drought (sections 9.2-9.3) solely by citing other work (e.g., Wanders et al. 2014, Brocca et al. 2012, Babaeian et al. 2018, Cammalleri et al. 2016) and recommends that bridging surface-to-root-zone SM would aid irrigation and drought management (section 10). No own result on remote sensing delivering climate-resilient or risk-management outcomes. Q1 'no', hence Q2-Q9 'no'.
